pillar_reactions.evidence: Rep opened it on the prospect's own terms — 'In your particular case, mobility is going to be the foundation of the whole training... because of the tight hips, because of the knee injuries, and the disc' — and the prospect took it over and co-diagnosed: 'this will be the challenge. I know it will be a challenge for me. I know where is my problem... Not so much my knee, I think my hip, but it's like locked. Believe me, everything comes from hips.' He also volunteered the travel failure mode unprompted when the rep raised portability.

Went further than the pillar asked. Offered to skip the weekly free meal entirely — 'I think I will keep myself away from that for a while. Then when I see results, then I can cheat a little bit. Until then, I don't want to cheat' — and volunteered his own carbohydrate insight: 'I was like a more anxious and more... Like more nervous, getting upset in a way or another.' The rep had to talk him down from over-restricting, which is an unusual direction for this pillar.

Rep tied it to the prospect's own history — 'You told me that you tried many times before... the problem is staying consistent when life gets busy' — plus Trevor's personal number, weekly check-ins and video form review. Prospect agreed firmly but without elaboration or questions: 'No, I should not. I would not. No, I would not. I don't want to.' Notable that the earlier permission ask ('do I have your permission to hold you accountable') drew a much warmer response than the pillar itself.

anchors.raw: even if we know we have good salaries here in Denmark. But either how, 9K is a lot of money, to be honest. It's not like a small amount, because it is a big amount. Even for Denmark, you we have a good salary and we have a good lifestyle
anchors.note: He concedes capacity in the same breath as objecting to size — the objection is to the number as a number, not to affordability. This is the point at which the financial picture should have been taken instead of the tier being cut.

anchors.raw: Either I choose you, and I go with you for a certain amount, even if I find another chance or somebody else... Either with you, either with somebody else. it's like, I need to, I need to do it anyhow.
anchors.note: He is buying the outcome regardless and shopping for the supplier. That makes the purchase highly likely and this specific deal replaceable, which is exactly the condition under which a verification request decides the sale. It was acknowledged and never addressed.

anchors.raw: maybe it is, it doesn't, it might be, sounds stupid. The cheaper version, but let's see what other alternatives we have to this.
anchors.note: An explicit request for a lower rung. The rep answered entirely from inside the price book — six months instead of twelve, a $3,000 renewal, and instalments — which is the third time in this batch the absence of a cheaper product forced improvisation.

anchors.raw: I think I watch it for the past. Three months, two months, three, months, I don't know. And he's doing a good job. You can see on him and he's having his good physique... if Trevor can do it, why we cannot do it? He's not a superhuman.
anchors.note: Months of free content built genuine belief in the coach before the call. The paradox worth noting is that this same prospect trusted Trevor on video and still would not release money to the company without a background check — the trust is in the person, not the business.

anchors.raw: I know the salespeople, you know, I'm also a sales guy, but here in Denmark, we don't do it in this way. We are, we give people time... Most salespeople, that's why they it up, because they want to do it right now, now, now, now.
anchors.note: Not a price anchor but a process anchor, and the decisive one. He sells for a living, recognised the deposit request as a closing device, and it converted a handshake into a delayed decision.

unmet_demand.want: Verifiable information about the company and the coach before releasing money — company details, background, and satisfied and unsatisfied customers
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing exists to send. The rep had to ask what was needed and could only agree to describe the business by email. For a prospect who runs background checks as routine practice, the absence of a credential or reference pack is the entire blocker, and no part of the offer addresses it.

unmet_demand.want: Month-to-month payment with no lock-in — 'I pay a month, I use a month. I pay a month, I use a month. I think this is fair enough for both of the parts'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is a fixed six- or twelve-month commitment paid up front or in financed instalments. The six-payment option looks like month-to-month but is a six-month contract at a higher total, so what he asked for and what he shook hands on are not the same product.
Only tier downgrades and instalments exist, and the instalments increase the total rather than lowering the commitment. Third occurrence of this gap in this batch.

unmet_demand.want: Training safely programmed around disc compression, an unstable knee and two years of untreated high blood pressure, with medical input
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No clinical pathway, no clearance step, and no evidence the programme can load this body safely. The rep instead framed the whole cluster as one lifestyle problem with one solution and forecast that the blood pressure would normalise. Whether the offer serves this prospect safely is undetermined and needs a human decision.
